newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar settles for weekend above 69 cents.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar settles for weekend above 69 cents.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended an uneventful day on Friday with its head just above 69 cents.
Dealers predict it will remain in a US$0.6880-0.6930 band over the weekend and early next week as the market prepares for the Reserve Bank's crucial June 27 Monetary Policy Statement.
At 5.15 p.m. (0515 GMT), the kiwi was at US 0.6902/09, having traded a 0.6880-0.6910 session range. The Trade-Weighted Index finished at 67.83, little changed from its opening.
Dealers said the market was characterised by offshore buying and local selling.
Foreign interest is still a hangover from recent eurokiwis while locals sold into the TWI following its overnight rise.
"The local market still thinks there is a good chance of an easing in the MPS and are happy to go short at 0.6890," said an Auckland dealer.
The Food Price Index fell 0.8 percent in May and that lack of inflationary pressure is seen giving further room for the Reserve Bank to ease.
